findings.claim: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy is non-monotone over the full observed window [0.0,0.49]: it rises to a positive peak near the middle of the window, then falls to a negative trough, then partially recovers toward zero. The observed-node linear fit is not accepted (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE≈0.78), so no single global linear trend describes this coordinate.

The endpoint rates of landmark_00_local_dx have opposite signs at the two ends of the window: first_rate_z is strongly negative and last_rate_z is strongly positive, with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches. This indicates the coordinate contrast is not stationary and its direction reverses within the observed support.

The whole-window mean of landmark_00_local_dx is near zero (whole_window_z≈-0.18), so the window-integrated level of this coordinate is close to the reference; the informative signal is in the within-window shape and endpoint rates rather than a net offset.

The score clock is defined on observed_score_times 0.0 to 0.49 with learning_window [0.0,0.5] and curve_support [0.0,0.49]; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior is used, so decoded final affinity is unobserved in this evidence.

hypotheses.direction: non-monotone; early positive excursion followed by a negative excursion and partial recovery
hypotheses.falsifier: A re-read of the same curve over the same support showing a monotone profile, or a held-out batch set in which the first and last rate signs agree, would falsify the non-monotone contrast claim.
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy shows a time-dependent contrast over the observed window: it is positive in the early-to-middle portion and negative in the later portion, with endpoint rates of opposite sign. This is an association between selection time and the coordinate proxy, not evidence of descendant survival or measured final benefit.

hypotheses.falsifier: Evidence that the whole-window mean is far from zero, or that first and last rates share a sign, would remove the need for a time-resolved contrast.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx whole-window mean versus first/last rate signs
hypotheses.statement: Because the whole-window mean of landmark_00_local_dx is near zero while the endpoint rates have opposite signs, a reward that targets only the window-integrated level of this coordinate would not distinguish the observed changing contrast from a stationary target; a time-resolved contrast would be needed to represent the observed shape.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves were read.
The curve is a coordinate proxy in predicted endpoint world-A features; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
Decoded final affinity labels are unobserved (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so no claim about final benefit or survival is made.
Only one feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read; other landmark coordinates were not queried and remain unobserved rather than absent.
The observed-node linear fit was not accepted and relative_node_RMSE is large, so the curve shape is described qualitatively rather than as a fitted polynomial.
